items.title: An $850,000 Portfolio in Park Hotels & Resorts, Healthpeak and Verizon Pays $51,477 a Year in Dividends. Here’s What Happens if One Cuts
items.summary: Key TakeawaysA $850,000 portfolio split evenly across Park Hotels & Resorts, Healthpeak Properties and Verizon pays about $4,290 a month in dividends at today’s prices. Each dividend is covered on its own measure: 51% of AFFO at Park, 72% of AFFO at Healthpeak, and 52% of free cash flow at Verizon.

items.summary: Chiron Real Estate shares rose 4.6% on Tuesday, Nov. 24, without company-specific news, as healthcare REITs gained and the S&P 500 fell.

items.title: The Roth IRA Mistake That Turns a 59-Year-Old’s $6,325 a Month in Tax-Free Dividends Into a Tax Bill
items.summary: A six-figure dividend paycheck inside your Roth sounds like the perfect retirement move, until the calendar gets involved. One overlooked timing rule can quietly turn your tax-free income into a tax bill and a penalty.

items.title: 3 Healthcare REITs Raised Their 2026 Outlooks as Senior Housing Demand Grows
items.summary: Baby boomers are turning 80, and three healthcare REITs just raised their 2026 guidance to capture the demand. Yet each dividend carries a cut in its past and a different risk, so which payout can retirees actually trust?

items.summary: Key TakeawaysA hypothetical $600,000 portfolio split evenly across Healthpeak Properties, Verizon and NNN REIT pays $37,054 a year in dividends at today’s prices, a 6. 2% yield.

items.title: Are Wall Street Analysts Predicting Healthpeak Properties Stock Will Climb or Sink?
items.summary: Healthpeak Properties has outperformed the broader market over the past year, and analysts are moderately optimistic about the stock’s prospects.

items.title: Doctors’ Offices, Labs and Nursing Homes Pay Rent to These 3 REITs, and $150,000 Yields $8,510 a Year
items.summary: Every clinic visit, rehab stay, and lab experiment ends with a rent check, and three healthcare landlords collect it. One has already cut its dividend twice, and another leans on Medicare dollars. Which one pays best, and what could break it?
